title: How De De improvises variations and departs from written parts
summary: De De says variations just come while playing, and that he swaps out written trumpet solos for his own.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: I was going to ask you about when you're up there playing by ear, how do you think of variations and everything?
Ah. That's a hard question. That just comes there, that's it.
It's just like it's in there, that's all I can tell you. That's all I can give it to you.
Well, do you play pretty much the same variation on a tune every time?
No. No, no. Sometimes I mimic a phrase in one, and then play that same song again, and something else come. Just like a gif, in other words. Yeah. That's all that, you know. Just come to it.
Well, how long before you can tell what the next thing is you play? Do you know before you play it, or do you know after you play it?
That's what comes to you after you make one, as you're playing. That comes along.

It just happens. It just comes. It just comes. A fellow make another note and you're right there with his father. That's what it is. Like you've been doing that all your life. It's something natural. Like a person talking, you know, just continue talking. That's the way that's done. The boys get to playing in the band like that, and get up and take a solo, and anything come to them, just put it in there. As long as I keep the melody, you know. That's right, isn't it? The in and out of it, you know?
Now what about some of these guys, it sounds to me like they play, they're trying to play variations. Do they play the same variation every night, or do they play it different? Different.
Some guys sound like they play.

They cannot play the same thing over and over and make the same variations, over again. They forget the same thing over again. That's quite natural to be written well and you have to follow it. Well I've seen some time in reading in the solo for the trumpet, I wouldn't put that song, I'd put my own in. You know what I mean?
Take it off the music. Even with the score you get off it? Yeah, get off it.

Get off it, oh yeah. Don't sound right to me like it's a score, you know? My imagination, that's what it is, you know? And if it doesn't sound better, well I'd put it in there than it's on the paper, time. And to me it does. That's how those things get in there. Yeah, you get a piece of music wrote and a trumpet solo and you don't like it, put another one in there. A couple of bars, or a different break or something like that, or your own.
